gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the Mobile Pixels Duex Max DS, ChatGPT's top pick for one USB-C port, has only a USB-C input and a mini-HDMI input and claims no pass-through charging, so on a laptop with one USB-C port its cable takes the only port; Aura's Single Boost Pro Max 15.6" ($199 at Aura's US store, 2026-11-21) also runs from one USB-C cable with no driver, and Aura says its second USB-C port charges the laptop at up to 45 W.
standout_why: Pages compared: itechguides 2025 (cited), The Office Journal's USB-C extenders guide (top result, run 2), Mobile Pixels' Trio page (cited, title and snippet only because of HTTP 429), and ChatGPT's own answers. itechguides lists 65 W pass-through for the Trio 3 Pro and warns that pass-through is 'not unlimited', so the idea is partly covered for the two-screen pick. None of them says the Duex Max DS has no second USB-C port for charging, and none names a single-screen extender that uses one USB-C cable with no driver and still charges the laptop. The Office Journal says that no product it lists passes power through. In run 1 ChatGPT names the Aura Dual Boost (driver, no pass-through stated) but never the Aura Single Boost.
decides: For a laptop that has one USB-C port and also charges through it, the Duex Max DS (ours) can't share that port with the charger. It stays the pick only for laptops that charge from a barrel or MagSafe plug, or for short sessions on battery. The Aura Single Boost Pro Max 15.6" wins the one-port, one-screen case on Aura's own claims. It is not a product we link and it is freestanding, not lid-mounted. The Trio 3 Pro (ours) is the two-screen answer from one port, but only with Mobile Pixels' driver. On base M1/M2/M3 MacBooks, the native-video path drives one external screen.
